canonical_name: libfec -- Phil Karn's forward-error-correction library (Viterbi + Reed-Solomon)
lineage: libfec (1995-, Phil Karn KA9Q): optimised VITERBI decoders for convolutional codes (the trellis / add-compare-select / traceback machinery) plus Reed-Solomon; the amateur-radio and deep-space FEC reference
version: github.com/ka9q/libfec master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
entry_points: the shipped vtest / vtest27 (Viterbi self-test); rstest (Reed-Solomon)

example.command: make && ./vtest27 (encode a random frame, add noise, Viterbi-decode)
example.input: a random bitstream + simulated channel noise
example.output: bit-error rate after decoding vs SNR

environment.obstruction_2026-09-12: libfec's Viterbi decoders ship hand-written 32-bit x86 MMX/SSE assembly (mmxbfly27.s: `push` with 32-bit suffixes) that will not assemble on x86-64, and its 1990s configure emits an invalid -march=x86_64. The portable C path (viterbi27_port.c) exists but the lib target forces the SIMD objects. A faithful run needs an i386 world (gcc -m32 / a 32-bit container) = RUNNABLE_HISTORICAL_TOOLCHAIN, queued. Source is pinned+hashed; nothing modernised. This is a preserved 'needs an old machine' fossil, not a failure.

human_capability_summary.built_to: recover the most-likely transmitted bit sequence from a noisy convolutionally-coded signal by the Viterbi algorithm (dynamic programming over a trellis of hidden encoder states), and to correct Reed-Solomon block errors
human_capability_summary.pressure: channel noise on band-limited links (satellite, deep space, radio); the decoder must find the maximum-likelihood path through an exponential state space in linear time
human_capability_summary.success_means: decoded bit-error rate at or below the code's theoretical curve for a given SNR; the self-tests pass

known_human_problem_solved: maximum-likelihood decoding of noisy coded signals (hidden-state estimation)

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run libfec-karn
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: recover the most-likely transmitted bit sequence from a noisy convolutionally-coded signal by the Viterbi algorithm (dynamic programming over a trellis of hidden encoder states), and to correct Reed-Solomon block errors
